text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A deadlock remains in the efforts of opposition parties to find a mutually acceptable candidate to run in the presidential elections early next year.
-Cyprus's economy has sturdy foundations, Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou tells the bank employees conference.
- Communist and socialist parties attending an international conference organised by (Cypriot communist) Akel party support the reunification and demilitarisation of Cyprus.
- A political scandal has broken out in the Russian foreign affairs ministry over the visit of members of the Russian Duma to Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus.
- Nicosia is formulating a proposal on the issue of Cyprus' presidency as a counter proposal to the Turkish side's demand for a rotating presidency.
- Pound notes with a new design are expected to go into circulation this month.
